findings.excerpt: @[scoped simp] theorem aMap_fst : aMap g G ≫ pullback.fst g g = pullback.fst (prodStr g g) g ≫ addMor g G := pullback.lift_fst _ _ _
findings.problem: The six `aMap`/`b1Map`/`b2Map` projection lemmas are tagged `@[scoped simp]` but have no `_assoc` (reassoc) variants. The goals they are meant for have the form `φ ≫ aMap g G ≫ pullback.fst g g`, and the bare lemma only fires when `aMap g G ≫ pullback.fst g g` is a literal subterm. Every later use rewrites by hand with `rw [Category.assoc, aMap_fst, ← Category.assoc, pullback.lift_fst, ...]` (lines 256, 264, 269, 290, 298, 303, 318, 323, 328). The `simp` attribute is therefore effectively unused. Mathlib's own `pullback.lift_fst` is `@[reassoc]` for this reason, and the new lemmas reduce to it.
findings.proposed_change: Mark each lemma `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`, with `scoped` on the simp part if the scoped behaviour is wanted. This generates `aMap_fst_assoc` and the rest, and registers them as simp lemmas. The `hα/hβ/hγ` side goals in `face₁`, `face₂`, `face₃` and `nonempty_pullback_rigSection_theta` can then use `simp`, or short `rw [Category.assoc, aMap_fst_assoc, ...]`, in place of the `Category.assoc`/`← Category.assoc` round trips. The rewrite direction is already correct and terminating, since the left-hand side is a composite through the defined map and the right-hand side no longer mentions it.
findings.benefit: The simp set becomes usable on composite goals. The repeated hand-written rewrite chains in the four theorems become shorter and no longer depend on the exact bracketing of `≫`. A reader can then see that the simp lemmas are used by the proofs.
